derivation: the smaller root of x^2 + b x + 1 is -1/b to leading order, and the unstable form computes it as (disc - b)/2, subtracting two numbers that agree to about log10(b^2/4) digits. The declared floor of 1e-7 is a magnitude the true root never falls below inside the domain until b reaches 1e7, where -1/b itself is -1e-7; measured crossing on this machine: b = 10000488.26 with one sign change, so the region is a clean interval rather than the ragged one a relative-error rule produces. A relative bound was tried first and rejected: the disagreement between two unstable forms is quantised by floating-point granularity, so it flickers over hundreds of crossings and cannot be declared as a box at all.

regions.reason: the unstable form has lost the root entirely and returns a value below the declared floor
